facts: The paper 'Agentic Code Reasoning' was authored by Shubham Ugare and Satish Chandra and released on arXiv on March 2, 2026 (arXiv:2603.01896).
The research investigates whether LLM agents can explore codebases and reason about code semantics without executing code.

The authors introduce semi-formal reasoning, a structured prompting methodology requiring agents to build explicit premises, trace execution paths, and derive formal conclusions acting as certificates.
For patch equivalence verification, semi-formal reasoning improves accuracy from 78% to 88% on curated examples and reaches 93% on real-world agent-generated patches.
For code question answering on RubberDuckBench (Mohammad et al., 2026), semi-formal reasoning achieves 87% accuracy.
For fault localization on Defects4J (Just et al., 2014), semi-formal reasoning improves Top-5 accuracy by 5 percentage points over standard reasoning.
The findings suggest execution-free semantic analysis can provide practical reliability for RL reward signals, code review, and static program analysis.
